newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten welcomes British passports for HK minorities.
newsitem.headline: Patten welcomes British passports for HK minorities.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten warmly welcomed London's decision on Tuesday to grant passports to an estimated 8,000 ethnic minority residents threatened with becoming stateless when the territory reverts to Chinese rule.
"This is an excellent Chinese New Year present to Hong Kong," Patten said in a statement released late on Tuesday night.
"The case has been put with dignity and vigour, and tonight the right decision has been made."
Patten said the British decision removed the question mark over the nationality of non-Chinese residents of Hong Kong after the territory reverts to China in five months' time.

"Without this pledge, their status after 30 June 1997 would have been uncertain: entitled to right of abode in Hong Kong without Chinese nationality and to British nationality without the right of abode in Britain," he said.

The decision affects some 8,000 people mostly of Indian and Pakistani origin, many of whose families have lived in the colony for generations but who hold only British travel documents and have not been entitled to settle or work in Britain.

While they will have residency rights in Hong Kong after the handover, whether they would be entitled to Chinese nationality and the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passports is so far not clear.
Patten along with representatives of the non-Chinese community have long argued that Britain has a responsibility to those threatened with becoming stateless.
